originalUnit.behavior: LSC-2P finding F1, security half (owner decisions 2026-10-25 items 1, 2 and 6): the server decides who may save or delete a live co-op campaign record from the verified bearer, never from the request body. Today PUT /api/campaigns/[id] treats an envelope whose body.coopSession is {mode:"host", matchId} as the live host's own save (isLiveHostSave, [id].ts:141), so a guest profile that adopted the host-shaped record can overwrite it, the live host adopts the write and broadcasts it to the legitimate guest, and an anonymous DELETE answers 204 and removes the row. After this unit, while CampaignHostRegistry.liveEntryFor(id) holds a live host entry, PUT is accepted only when the request carries a bearer that verifies and whose principal is that entry's host, and DELETE is refused for everyone, the host's own included, until the session ends (owner ruling applied under the standing instruction; it changes the prep draft LW09); a member or guest bearer, an expired, malformed or absent bearer and a body-only coopSession are refused with a typed code and reason (HOST_SESSION_REQUIRED when there is no usable bearer, HOST_SESSION_EXPIRED when it expired; a verified non-host PUT keeps today's 409 live-coop-session conflict, owner decisions 2026-10-25b Q2 item 6), and the record, its version and the live host are untouched and nothing is broadcast. The host's browser store attaches its stored co-op bearer to record PUT; CampaignDashboardPage.tsx shows the server's refusal when Delete Campaign is refused while a session runs. The save-status card shows the server's refusal reason, keeps the unsaved changes and the dirty flag, and no longer labels a refusal "playing offline; changes are kept locally" (S4-03, refusal display only). Acceptance rows, each a failing test first: host same-tab reload (the bearer is still in sessionStorage) saves 200; host in a new window without the token is refused with the typed reason, the save card shows it and the unsaved changes are kept (disclosed: a new window cannot save a running co-op campaign, the host keeps its original window); app restart before any member reconnects (no live entry) takes the offline path and is accepted, pinned; app restart after a guest reconnected (entry live again) is refused as in the new-window row; expired host token takes the refresh path then 200, or a typed re-unlock refusal, never "kept locally"; offline host (no live entry): PUT and DELETE from another profile are accepted, pinned as disclosed behaviour so a later change is deliberate; a guest mirror save of its own record is unchanged; any DELETE while a host is live is refused, the host's own included, and works again after the session ends. Out of scope: the display half (a fresh profile rendering the HOST badge and host review surface), which owner decision 2 rewords out of Step 2 and discloses; record-scoped authority when the host is offline, the viewer-relative GET projection and the host re-authentication path, which stay with B15-3R and B15-3 after v2.2.0. The rule is keyed on the verified principal, not on a window or tab, so it does not preclude multi-window state for one identity (owner decision 6; MULTI-WINDOW-SESSION-1). It absorbs the host-save bearer attach and the live-host write rule of B15-2 and B15-3 by annotation only; neither is a predecessor.

review.body:
VERDICT: REPAIR-REQUIRED
reviewedHead: ca5786ca3c858bab22522bbe6e5631276fe42916
reviewedSourceHead: 4f40acfd86e1e8cf43c4d4b3f1e7d4b3b64516f7
reviewerModel: gpt-6.1-sol

reviewContract: unversioned, campaign-only; no v2/v3 attestation

We are reviewing MekStation, a BattleTech tabletop game construction and gameplay companion. This is authorized maintenance and testing of the owner's game repository and its local development/test instances. Combat, attacks, weapons, damage, targets and fog of war describe game mechanics; API, WebSocket, identity and permission checks concern the game's own multiplayer and desktop services.

P1 — Host match-close acknowledges success without ending its campaign session; this blocks CAMPAIGN-LIVE-WRITE-1 closure.

The failure is a valid public-route lifecycle regression seam. The probe's expectation is supported by the shipped contract, not an invented interpretation of DELETE. openspec/specs/multiplayer-server/spec.md:282-287 explicitly says the host's DELETE marks the match completed and sends connected clients a Close envelope. src/pages/api/multiplayer/matches/[id].ts:8 calls this a host-only close. The registered CAMPAIGN-LIVE-WRITE-1 behavior and its registration20261025bCorrection require live DELETE refusal followed by successful deletion after the session ends. The campaign API itself tells users to end the session before deleting. A successful explicit close that cannot release the live guard fails that outcome.

Evidence and causal trace

1. I inspected the clean detached checkout at the requested merged head, tree 489b7acfcf8ccb939d9d09429350e453f856e796, with ordered parents 34d9abf320725475e890f999bca508a275a748d7 and 4f40acfd86e1e8cf43c4d4b3f1e7d4b3b64516f7. Read-only git diff confirms the three close/registry files named in production-close-finding.json are unchanged across #2399. This establishes provenance, not a baseline runtime result or an exemption.
2. Read production-close-finding.json, production-live-r2/result.json, its playwright.log and writes.jsonl, production-live-write.spec.ts, production-live.playwright.config.cjs, production-live.cjs, build/result.json, and relevant base Playwright configuration. The log fails specifically at production-live-write.spec.ts:39, after match DELETE succeeded at :37-38. The exact response names match 51848804-30d4-4207-9320-24430815bec7 and returns 401 HOST_SESSION_REQUIRED, reason malformed, with the message to end the live session first. The recorder independently shows campaign create 200, match create 201, authenticated host save 200, anonymous save 401, anonymous live delete 401, host live delete 403, host match close 200, then campaign delete 401 twice (the second is finally cleanup). The preceding GET equality assertion passed because execution reached the close.
3. The production run used NODE_ENV=production and the existing standalone image. Its before-image hashes equal build/result.json's image for BUILD_ID 1793331822200. I independently rehashed the thirteen recorded source/config paths and five recorded standalone image paths: zero mismatches against the run's after hashes. The result records exit 1, one unexpected test, zero skipped/flaky, unchanged source/image, and portReusable true for port 56787. These are existing proof observations, not a new test run by this reviewer. The configuration still supplies ordinary Playwright run/storage/E2E environment values; “unflagged” describes the built image, not an absence of every test-harness environment variable. The inspected close/create/registry code contains no E2E branch that explains away this outcome.
4. Match POST registers the campaign entry before returning 201 (src/pages/api/multiplayer/matches/index.ts:343-364), while the new match starts as lobby (:234). The HTTP-only probe never creates a tactical socket host. Match DELETE authenticates and verifies the actual host, then calls only getMatchHostRegistry().closeMatch(id) and returns 200 ([id].ts:120-151). MatchHostRegistry.ts:255-261 returns immediately when there is no tactical host. It neither completes the stored match nor disposes the campaign entry in this case. A tactical host's own close does complete storage (ServerMatchHost.ts:1163-1189), but likewise has no campaign teardown here.
5. CampaignHostRegistry.liveEntryFor considers every matching nonclosed host live, including a paused GM-absent session (:409-419). Its entry.close unregisters the active host, closes arbiter/host and clears participation state (:254-260); dispose removes the entry (:478-483). My source searches found disposal callers only in tests. Campaign DELETE consults liveEntryFor and refuses before persistence (src/pages/api/campaigns/[id].ts:458-489). Thus the observed refusal is exactly the product code's predicted consequence. The probe did not GET match metadata after close; “still lobby” is a source inference, not an additional observed HTTP result.

What genuinely ends a session

A terminal host close must stop its authority; removing a tab or losing the GM connection is not terminal. bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:1231-1235 invokes noteGmDisconnected, which deliberately pauses and preserves the session (CampaignSyncSession.ts:297-331). The terminal hostDisconnected method closes the host (:880-889), but my searches found only test callers. CampaignMatchHost.close (:263-276) is terminal, but the acceptance tests call it directly rather than reaching it through the public close route.

LW09 in campaignCoopRecordAuthz.test.ts:426-454 proves refusal then calls entry.host.close() at :449. LW11 does the same at :476-483. Those are valid guard-unit tests and insufficient lifecycle integration proof. The existing two-browser journey's cleanup closes the match and accepts 200/404 (e2e/coop-campaign-two-browser-journey.spec.ts:486-499); it does not assert campaign deletion or the resulting terminal campaign state. Its prior PASS cannot establish this contract.

Restart-before-reconnect remains an explicitly disclosed offline acceptance boundary (LW10 resets the registry at :460). It is not an acceptable replacement for host-close behavior. A member can reconstitute the campaign entry from durable co-op metadata (CampaignHostRegistry.ts:422-475); GM absence is intentionally recoverable. Requiring a process restart and a race against reconnect would conceal the explicit-close gap. This review does not reopen the separately accepted offline record-authority residual or demand B15-3R early.

Smallest justified repair and proof

Keep the existing live campaign DELETE guard and its refusal assertions. Repair server lifecycle ownership, not its callers' expectations. A one-line dispose in the route is insufficient: it leaves durable match state open and permits getOrCreate to recreate the entry, since createEntry currently checks coopCampaign but not completed status (:453-475). It also does not fulfill the Close-envelope requirement for campaign sockets.

A concrete narrow candidate is four existing production leaves:

- src/pages/api/multiplayer/matches/[id].ts: after the existing authentication/host check, await the complete terminal close and campaign teardown before returning success. Compose public lifecycle contracts; do not reach into private maps or weaken authorization.
- src/lib/multiplayer/server/MatchHostRegistry.ts: complete the stored match even when no tactical host was created; retain existing tactical socket cleanup. Refuse recreation of a completed match and preserve close-during-bootstrap ordering. Existing IMatchStore.closeMatch already provides durable/idempotent completion, so no schema/store rewrite is justified.
- src/lib/multiplayer/server/CampaignHostRegistry.ts: own terminal campaign disposal and close notification/cleanup registration, drain or invalidate in-flight reconstruction, and prevent completed matches from rebuilding. Keep a normal GM disconnect recoverable. A closed entry must not return as usable authority.
- src/lib/multiplayer/server/bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts: connect each bound socket's existing cleanup/Close path to the shared entry's terminal lifecycle. Its socketsByMatch Map and campaignSocketLifecycles WeakMap are module-local (:223-231). Merely exporting a function that reads the API graph's copy of those maps will miss sockets in server.js's separate module graph. Use the existing shared entry to carry the actual teardown callbacks; do not add a parallel global registry or broad transport redesign.

This is a bounded candidate footprint, not an implemented patch or a frozen line estimate. A smaller implementation is acceptable only if it proves all these postconditions. No new UI, protocol/schema, database migration, dependency, generated file, shared E2E helper, or campaign record-auth change is justified by this finding. Do not end a still-running campaign merely because a separate coopMission tactical match completed; target the exact campaign-session match ID. Existing tactical close callers must retain their semantics.

Use existing tests rather than a new framework. The likely minimum durable test footprint is MatchHostRegistry.closeRoute.test.ts, CampaignHostRegistry.test.ts, and campaignCoopRecordAuthz.test.ts (seven source/test leaves total with the four above). Extend the cross-module close-route coverage to real campaign binding and teardown; extend registry coverage for completed metadata and a deferred reconstruction racing close. In the campaign authorization suite retain guard-unit tests and add a real match-create -> live campaign refusal -> host match DELETE -> campaign DELETE integration case. Never call host.close/dispose/reset to achieve the post-close assertion.

The essential regression must reproduce the HTTP-only, no-tactical-host case; verify anonymous/non-host close preserves both registries and record, host close returns 200 only after durable completed status and no live campaign entry, and campaign DELETE then returns 204 and GET 404 under the accepted offline rule. Add a connected campaign host/guest variant: both receive Close and cleanup runs, no later command commits, and a new connection cannot resurrect the ended session, including after a fresh-process reopen of the same databases. Repeat close should preserve the established idempotent behavior. Cover the bounded close/recovery race because both registries reconstruct asynchronously; a delayed creation must not restore live authority after close acknowledges completion.

Affected consumers include the campaign DELETE/live save guard, match GET/list/invite/reconnect paths through metadata, the campaign binder, and existing match-close cleanup in the two-browser journey and GM pack specs. The registered cleanup census also names e2e/fixtures/campaign.ts:392-399 and e2e/gm-campaign-ledger-control-plane.spec.ts:120-131; both throw on unsuccessful anonymous deletion. Recheck applicable scenarios after repair. Their edits are not automatically required or granted. Avoid a shared-helper edit unless a real failing caller requires it; DELIVERY.md would then require all importing ladder groups to rerun.

Root should preserve this failed production proof, get red-first regression evidence on the actual public route, then run focused lifecycle/auth suites and applicable static checks, CI, fresh independent exact-head reviews and sensitive head-bound owner ruling. Build and repeat the production route probe plus the connected cross-module case on the exact repair merge; preserve initial source/image identity, real credentials, isolated stores, owned listener and cleanup. This reviewer ran no tests, server or build. Historical 75/75, 122/122 and browser counts are not repair-head proof.

Scope and budget consequence

The current unit's caps are 15 files/500 counted additions. Its approved publicationLayout20261030 enumerates exactly ten source/test leaves plus five implementation lifecycle leaves, with zero slack; actual #2399 changed exactly fifteen files. These lifecycle production leaves are outside registeredSourceLeaves and the frozen implementation manifest. The merged PR cannot be enlarged retrospectively, and the pending publication 5 was planned for campaign closure plus next-unit admission, not unregistered lifecycle source. Root must record this unresolved acceptance obligation and register/admit a measured repair scope before product edits. Neither historical file headroom nor the broader directory navigation grants extra leaves.

Step 4's actual approved budget is 29 PRs, with campaign admission/source/closure allocated positions 3/4/5. The admission ownerDecision.accepted.publication explicitly says no extra PR budget. At least one additional product PR is now necessary; there is no evidence of a spare slot. If registration/admission uses the pending publication 5, followed by repair source and then campaign closure/desktop admission, that plan consumes 5/6/7 instead of the former closure at 5: +2 publications and a projected 31 rather than 29 absent measured savings elsewhere. A separately authorized, concretely fitting combined publication could reduce that delta; this review grants neither that combination nor a budget increase. Freeze/count the actual manifests and identify the real offset or obtain the required budget/scope correction. Full-send authorizes Root's delivery work; it does not make these ungranted paths or extra slots already approved. Do not close CAMPAIGN-LIVE-WRITE-1 or begin successor implementation to hide this debt.

Verification limits and observed review state

Review only; the assigned report is my only write. No subagents, product/evidence edits, tests, servers, builds, Git writes or GitHub writes. Final source status remained clean at the requested head. I did not independently rerun the baseline or production failure, prove whole-tree merge equality anew, audit every #2399 behavior, or verify absence of every surviving process. The recorded reusable port supports listener release, not universal process cleanup. No provider refusal occurred in this review. Model/harness/effort above are runtime-declared; backend routing, subscription identity and independent engine attestation are not established by this report. Root must bind actual T3 observations for the approved unversioned provenance transport.
